Not verified: the Oct 1 'end of Russia-Ukraine talks' headline, the Oct 20 Sherritt fuel permission (no web trace; I could not tell whether it is a license), the Oct 8 'US and Russia discuss reviving Russian gas sales to Europe' item (the headline matches a May 2025 Reuters story, so it may be a mis-dated re-crawl), the EU 22nd sanctions package outcome (ambassadors were to try on Oct 7) and the Oct 8 India Russian-flows 310k bpd figure that conflicts with Kpler's 1.8-1.9M bpd. Asia coverage is thin: Japan/India/Korea candidates were mostly equity-flow and jobs stories, and I found no verified China property, deflation or export-control event in the 240.
gaps.iran_energy: Biggest unmapped storylines: (1) the state of the 'fire pause' itself - the tree defines it by US/Iranian strike nights, but IRGC tanker attacks, Houthi strikes on Riyadh and Dhahran and a claimed US strike near Sirik on 10/21 are happening inside it, so no node can say whether the pause has ended; (2) Houthi-Saudi war and Saudi bypass capacity (East-West pipeline, Yanbu) - only three nodes (houthi-saudi, red-sea-front, es-anchor) cover it and none is priced on actual Saudi output or export data; (3) US domestic fuel policy (G7/IEA releases, GL 135 Russian diesel, diesel export-ban talk, $6.28 diesel) has no home in the tree and is partly captured by new ev- nodes. Could not verify: the Brent five-month high on 10/20 (feed only; the 10/22 price is confirmed), the 10/22 Iranian tanker claims (the claim is verified, the damage is not), the Hurricane Isaias landfall category, and the 10/16 Saudi 'attacks cut output' feed item, which is an April 2026 Reuters story re-surfaced; I also found no web confirmation of Trump accusing Iran of faking ship strikes (single CBS headline). The candidate file also contained much syndication of the same tanker-attack wire stories and many Indian market wraps that I merged or dropped; Sunday-night and weekend events may be under-dated by a day.
